comparisons.peer_topic: Chief Information Officer Committee Composition and Function
comparisons.peer_summary: The Chief Information Officer Committee serves as an escalation forum for technology senior management, including policy approval, and reports items to the Board's Technology Committee as appropriate.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Citigroup (C) disclose specific executive committees focused on technology and digital risk governance that report to broader technology risk committees or the Board. GS establishes the 'Digital Risk Office Steering Group' to oversee Engineering risk decisions and regulatory compliance, co-chaired by the CISO, CTO, and Chief Digital Risk Officer, with reporting lines to the Firmwide Technology Risk Committee. Similarly, Citi establishes the 'Chief Information Officer Committee (CIOC)' as an escalation forum for technology senior management, including the CISO, to approve policies and report items to the Board's Technology Committee. Both structures utilize specific C-suite leaders (including CISOs) to steer technical risk execution and policy approval within a hierarchy reporting to higher-level technology governance bodies.

sentences.text: The Digital Risk Office Steering Group oversees Engineering risk decisions, monitors control performance and reviews approaches to comply with current and emerging regulation applicable to Engineering.
This steering group is co-chaired by our CISO, chief technology officer and chief digital risk officer, and reports to the Firmwide Technology Risk Committee.

The Chief Information Officer Committee (CIOC), which consists of, among others, the Head of Technology and Business Enablement, Citi's Co-Chief Information Officers (who report to the Head of Technology and Business Enablement), the CISO, and the Head of TCCORO (who reports both to Citi's Head of Operational Risk within the Risk organization and its Head of Global Functions Compliance within the Global Legal and Compliance organization), serves as an escalation forum for items requiring the attention of technology senior management, including approval of policies, and reports items requiring further escalation to the Technology Committee of the Board of Directors, as appropriate.

comparisons.peer_topic: Board and Committee Oversight of Cybersecurity
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's Board of Directors receives periodic updates from the CIO, CISO, and senior CTOC members concerning cybersecurity matters, including developments, policies, initiatives, and significant incidents. The Audit Committee and Risk Committee assist the Board in this oversight, while the Global Technology Operating Committee (GTOC) governs the Firmwide Global Technology organization and resolves key operational risk matters.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) detail the structure of board-level oversight for cybersecurity and technology risks, highlighting the role of the Board and its committees in receiving updates from executive leadership. GS discloses that its digital and AI risk steering groups report to the 'Firmwide Technology Risk Committee,' which oversees technology matters. JPM explicitly states that the Firm's Board of Directors receives periodic updates directly from the CIO, CISO, and CTOC regarding cybersecurity matters, with assistance from the Audit and Risk Committees. While GS focuses on the intermediate reporting line to a Technology Risk Committee and JPM on direct Board updates via specific officers, both peers illustrate a governance model where technology executives drive the reporting flow to high-level oversight bodies for cybersecurity and technology policy.

sentences.text: To assist the Firmwide Technology Risk Committee in carrying out its mandate, the Firmwide Artificial Intelligence Risk and Controls Committee, which oversees risks associated with the use of AI, reports to the Firmwide Technology Risk Committee.
This steering group is co-chaired by our CISO, chief technology officer and chief digital risk officer, and reports to the Firmwide Technology Risk Committee.

As part of its oversight of management's implementation and maintenance of the Firm's risk management framework, the Firm's Board of Directors receives periodic updates from the CIO, the CISO and senior members of the CTOC concerning cybersecurity matters.

The GTOC is responsible for the governance of the Firmwide Global Technology organization, including oversight of Firmwide technology strategies, the delivery of technology and technology operations, the effective use of information technology resources, and monitoring and resolving key operational risk and control matters arising in the Global Technology organization.

peer_results.rationale: Candidate disclosures (ms_2024_7_D211, ms_2024_7_D370) focus on the Firm Risk Committee's oversight of the general ERM framework and the Board Risk Committee's oversight of climate risk. These topics are distinct from the specific cybersecurity and AI technology governance committees detailed in the target disclosure.
